R7BL-bear-backcountry-0001.name: By Thinahtea Creek
R7BL-bear-backcountry-0001.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R7BL-bear-backcountry-0001.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed gravel road

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2013 (13 years old), 370 m E: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2023 (fire G90288), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
Thinahtea Creek 20 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Northern Rockies Regional Municipality, about 282 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 59.92974, -120.06961, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 5.1 km SE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 5 m, about 102 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 100 m E of the spot at 459 m (59.89471, -120.00951). Water: Thinahtea Creek 70 m W (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-55, Region 7B. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2020-02-25, closures 2026-10-16.
